description: We are a team of high school and middle school students (ages 15 and 13) who share a passion for astronomy, chemistry, coding, and hand-drawn comics. We enjoy combining science, technology, and art to tell creative stories and explore new ideas.
summary:
WAYFINDERS: They Will Not Be Forgotten is an original, five-page, hand-drawn science-fiction comic that brings the stories of three retired NASA explorers left behind on Mars (Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity) to life for school-age space enthusiasts.

In 2076, a powerful solar storm disables Earth's GPS systems. At a Mars colony, an astronaut and a robot revisit these explorers' histories, looking for lessons that could help restore navigation on Earth.

Readers discover what each machine was built to do and what it accomplished: Sojourner pioneered rover exploration and obstacle detection; Opportunity uncovered evidence of ancient water and used visual odometry and autonomous route planning; and Ingenuity demonstrated powered flight and sensor-based aerial navigation without GPS. Their successes and limitations inspire a fictional, more resilient navigation system.

We also tell this story through traditional comic-making techniques: pencil drawing, hand inking, and adhesive screentone paper. In a world increasingly shaped by digital technology and AI, these techniques risk being overlooked and forgotten. Like the Mars explorers, they deserve to be remembered and passed on.

WAYFINDERS connects the legacy of space hardware with the enduring value of hands-on art, inviting young readers to explore both science and creativity.
details:
Our Project

WAYFINDERS is an original five-page, hand-drawn educational science-fiction comic created for NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026's "Abandoned but Not Forgotten" challenge.

Our goal is to introduce school-age readers to three historic NASA explorers left behind on Mars, Sojourner, Opportunity, and Ingenuity, through an imaginative adventure that combines real scientific discoveries, engineering achievements, and futuristic storytelling.

Rather than simply presenting historical facts, we connect these three explorers through a common scientific challenge: How can robots navigate without GPS?

Hand-Drawn Comic

Page 1: The Crisis Begins

In 2076, a powerful solar storm disables Earth's GPS systems, causing a global navigation crisis. Researchers turn to historic Mars explorers for inspiration.

Page 2: Sojourner

Sojourner pioneered robotic exploration on Mars in 1997, analyzing Martian rocks and using onboard sensors to detect obstacles while revealing the limitations of early autonomous navigation

Page 3: Opportunity

Opportunity discovered evidence of ancient water on Mars and advanced robotic navigation through stereo vision, visual odometry, and autonomous route planning.

Page 4: Ingenuity

Ingenuity achieved the first powered, controlled flight on another planet, using cameras and onboard sensors to navigate without GPS. Its final flight also revealed the limitations of visual navigation over featureless terrain.

Page 5: Solving Earth's Crisis

Inspired by all three explorers, the characters envision a resilient GPS-free navigation system to help Earth recover from its crisis. The story concludes by honoring the lasting legacy of these pioneering Mars robots.
